`subscribe` and `join` are DIFFERENT message types. `subscribe` is for table CRUD events (uses `tables:[...]`); `join` is for room broadcasts (uses `room:`). Mixing them silently no-ops.
Same-origin enforced server-side - cross-origin WebSocket attempts return 403.

`/ws` returns 401 to anonymous clients when the app has auth configured. The WebSocket handshake carries the session cookie same-origin, so being logged-in is enough. Set `features.ws_anonymous: true` in app.yaml to drop the gate - covers `/sse/events` simultaneously.

Table-change events are owner/group-scoped server-side. Subscribers only see detailed `{table, action}` events when they're the owner (for owner-scoped tables) or in the same group (for group-scoped via `groups:`). Non-matching subscribers in an owner-scoped scenario get `{action:'refresh'}` with no table - a hint to refetch a server-scoped list without learning which row. Admins always see the detail.
For one-way data-event invalidation use SSE instead - simpler protocol, auto-reconnects, less protocol churn.

WebRTC over this transport works - see `webrtc_pattern` above for the perfect-negotiation skeleton + the three subtle bugs that cause first-frame-then-freeze (wrong stream binding, dropped early ICE candidates, and glare).

Verify end-to-end with the MCP tool `probe_route(app, path:'/api/_auth/profile', as:'alice@example.com', keep_session:true)` (CLI: `benmore probe <app> GET /api/_auth/profile --as alice@example.com --keep-session`) to mint a cookie, then a follow-up curl with that cookie to /ws or /sse/events. Without keep_session the session dies on probe return; with it, it lasts 5 minutes.

Frontend cache: served HTML rewrites `/static/` references in href, src, poster, srcset/imagesrcset and an og:image `content` to `?v=<content hash>`, so a push gets past Cloudflare's cache (it can keep a /static/ URL for about a day whatever the origin sends). A .js version hashes every file under static/, so an edit to an imported .tsx, .json, .css or text file changes it. The framework replaces any `?v=` you write; another query string (`?hash=…`) turns the rewrite off for that reference. Only the URL carrying the current version is cached for a year; link to static files from pages, not by bare URL, when freshness after a push or promote matters.

`features.ws: false` in app.yaml turns the endpoint off: `/ws` is not served, so the handshake fails and bm.room and `/ws` table subscriptions cannot connect. It is on by default. `/sse/events` has its own switch, `features.sse`.
